Package org.aristonis.diwan.database.event

Class ConnectionEvents

java.lang.Object
org.aristonis.diwan.database.event.ConnectionEvents
public final class ConnectionEvents extends Object
Registers listeners, keeps the query log and runs the slow-query handlers of one connection family.

A root connection and every session, transaction and scope derived from it share one instance, returned by Connection.events(). Registration is safe from any thread, even while statements run.

While a listener or handler runs, statements the same thread runs on the connection fire no events and are not logged, which rules out recursion and a log that grows by reading itself.

When nothing listens, no handler is set and the log is off, a statement costs nothing extra: the connection reads no clock and builds no event.

Instances are safe to share between threads.

    • getQueryLog

      public List<LoggedQuery> getQueryLog()
      Returns a copy of the query log, oldest entry first.
      Returns:
      an unmodifiable list, never null
      API Note:
      The log keeps at most the limit set with ConnectionBuilder.queryLogLimit(int); the oldest entries are dropped first. Binding values are stored compactly: a byte[] appears as <byte[n]> and a string over 1024 characters is cut and ends with ...(n chars). When the connection was built with showBindingsInErrors(false), no binding value is kept: each one appears as ?.

      public Registration whenQueryTakesLongerThan(Duration threshold, Consumer<QueryExecuted> handler)
      Calls a handler for each statement that took longer than a threshold.
      Parameters:
      threshold - the limit, never null and not negative; a statement must take strictly longer
      handler - the handler, never null; it runs on the thread that ran the statement
      Returns:
      a handle that removes the handler, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if threshold is negative

    • whenQueryingForLongerThan

      public Registration whenQueryingForLongerThan(Duration threshold, BiConsumer<Connection,QueryExecuted> handler)
      Calls a handler once when the statements of this family have taken longer than a threshold in total.
      Parameters:
      threshold - the limit, never null and not negative
      handler - the handler, never null; it runs on the thread that ran the statement
      Returns:
      a handle that removes the handler, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if an argument is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if threshold is negative
      API Note:
      The handler runs for the statement that pushes the total past the threshold and then stays quiet until resetTotalQueryDuration(). It receives the connection that ran that statement.

    • executed

      @Internal public void executed(Connection source, QueryExecuted event)
      Records a successful statement and tells the listeners and handlers about it.

      Every listener and handler runs. If any failed, the first failure is thrown after all ran, wrapped in a ListenerFailedException, with the others suppressed onto it. An Error from a listener does not skip the others; the first failure being an Error, it is thrown as it is, with the others suppressed onto it.

      Parameters:
      source - the connection the statement ran on, never null
      event - the finished statement, never null

    • failed

      @Internal public void failed(QueryFailed event)
      Tells the listeners a statement failed. Any Throwable a listener throws is suppressed onto the event's exception, and the remaining listeners still run.
      Parameters:
      event - the failed statement, never null

    • transaction

      @Internal public void transaction(TransactionPhase phase, TransactionEvent event)
      Tells the listeners about a transaction step.

      A failure during TransactionPhase.COMMITTING propagates at once. In every other phase all listeners run, then the first failure is thrown with the others suppressed onto it.

      Parameters:
      phase - the transaction step, never null
      event - the transaction, never null
